# Sprint1 - grooming and planning meeting -- 2026-09-03

Scheduled 14:00 to 15:00 UTC (09:00 to 10:00 CDT), organiser Rajeev Kumar. The
invite body: "As we're almost at the end of Shape (discovery) phase. I'm
setting up this meeting for Sprint1 grooming and planning discussion." The
transcript was recorded 13:59:50 to 14:54:37 UTC and the cues run 00:00:08 to
00:54:47, so the call used about 55 of its 60 minutes. Bounteous-internal, no
client attendees. Invited: Rajeev Kumar, Pramod Kumar, Pankaj Aggarwal, Nitish
Goyal, Neelesh Aggarwal, Manish Mehra, Karuna Arshakota, Shubhankar Bhavsar,
Chahat Sharma, Rob Forshier II. Six people speak, and the frontmatter lists
those six.

**Pankaj Aggarwal did not attend.** Rajeev flagged the conflict in his opening
(00:01:27). His absence shaped the outcome: SCRIBL-21, the API contract and
mock server, the auth and onboarding epic, the moderation decision and the
whole spike set were all parked on him, and Rajeev cut sprint 2 planning short
because of the gap (00:51:51: "Pankaj is not there in the meeting and that is
creating a gap also").

The daily standup ran immediately after at 15:00 UTC. Digest at
[2026-09-03-standup.md](2026-09-03-standup.md).

Timestamps are offsets into the raw transcript.

## Decisions

- **Transcription only, no video recording.** Rajeev asked at 00:00:35. Rob,
  00:00:44: "as long as we transcribe, that's fine... I think transcription is
  at least enough." Rajeev agreed, 00:00:50.
- **Nomenclature: sprint 1, 2, 3, 4, following Jira. Drop "sprint zero".**
  Rajeev, 00:23:23: "from today onwards, let's talk about Sprint one, two,
  three, and four. Let's forget about Sprint zero. I know in our SOW, it is a
  Sprint zero, but we will stick with Jira nomenclature, right, to avoid any
  confusion." Owner Rajeev. This landed after Rob himself tripped on it at
  00:23:20 ("I was thinking it was a sprint zero, my bad").
- **No features layer between epics and stories. Run epic -> story, with
  tasks and subtasks under stories where needed.** Rajeev, 00:07:49: "if we
  need, we can introduce features in between, between epics and user story...
  But as we already started, we are in the middle, let's move forward... it
  should not impact us." Owner Rajeev. The trigger was Rob flagging his own
  setup at 00:04:23 and again at 00:05:22: "I created a feature in a user
  story. I just didn't set up the hierarchy right. So right now you can't
  create a user story and have its parent be a feature because I didn't
  configure Jira to do that and I didn't know how to do that." Epics, features,
  spikes and user stories currently all sit at the same work-item level. Rob
  asked whoever knows how to fix it to fix it; Rajeev decided not to.
- **The sprint calendar. Sprint 1 still ends tomorrow, 2026-09-04.** This is
  the decision that matters most for the Shape Review, and it was contested.
  Pramod opened it at 00:14:10: "there was that slight aberration, Rob, that
  where we had that seven day shape and the three sprints. Do we still keep
  that?" and noted "Jira currently shows September 4th as the sprint end"
  (00:15:00). He then argued the client is short-changed, 00:17:03: "if we have
  it as seven and seven day sprint followed by three, two week sprints. We may
  be a bit short of what the client was entitled for", and asked directly,
  00:17:16: "do you think from that perspective it makes sense to just have it
  as a full two-week sprint for shape?" Rob offered to move the review,
  00:18:35: "with some individuals being out tomorrow, I would actually lean
  towards, if we want to, I can move the shape review till later on next week."
  **The two-week shape option was raised and NOT taken.** Pramod closed it
  himself at 00:19:17: "tomorrow, yeah, tomorrow seems like a logical this
  thing." Rob double-checked late in the call, 00:44:16: "did we align on the
  end of our shape sprint? Are we saying shape ends tomorrow like I have it
  currently set?" Pramod, 00:44:28: "No, tomorrow was what we said, ending
  tomorrow, Rajeev."
  - Sprint 1 (shape/discovery): ends 2026-09-04.
  - Sprint 2: 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-18.
  - Sprint 3: to 2026-10-02.
  - Sprint 4: to 2026-10-16, "the logical conclusion of eight weeks project"
    (Rajeev, 00:18:05).
  - Rajeev framed the run as "from 24th August to two weeks each" (00:17:44).
    That is loose arithmetic: 24 August to 4 September is twelve days, not two
    weeks. The dates above are what the team agreed; the two-weeks-each framing
    is not literally true of sprint 1.
- **Skip the spikes in this session; Pankaj reviews and updates them later.**
  Rob, 00:27:44: "I feel like Pankaj has already done that one too. For right
  now, why don't we just skip the spikes and just focus on getting things added
  to sprint two and then just have Pankaj review these spikes when he has a
  minute... because I feel like he's done the majority of these or we have
  documentation for them already." He added at 00:28:03: "some of them I just
  created just to flush out like, hey, we might need this... and some of these
  we might not have needed." Rajeev accepted. SCRIBL-7 through SCRIBL-17 carry
  the E00 sprint-zero tag and are still in the backlog (Rajeev, 00:26:10).
- **Take the whole of epic SCRIBL-1 (cloud foundation and app shell) into
  sprint 2, rather than cherry-picking stories.** Rajeev, 00:36:21: "if we
  decide this entire scribble one, right, we are doing it in Sprint 2. It
  doesn't mean it has to end within Sprint 2. There will be something which
  might be left open which will roll over." Nitish owns the backend side of it
  (00:36:47, Nitish: "Yap"). Rob had pushed for the epic to be finished,
  00:35:39: "we still need to go through the epic one at the top there and make
  sure we get through all the epic one stuff."
- **Plan and progress at the epic level, not fine-grained tickets.** Rajeev's
  stated philosophy, and a real decision about how this team works. 00:33:53:
  "whatever we are doing as of now was traditional approach method, but looking
  at the uses of agentic AI... we should go at high level. Here, we will try to
  complete this epic all together in Sprint 2 or Sprint 3." At 00:47:13: "we
  may not focus too much on what we are doing in Jira versus what we are doing
  actually on the work front. Jira can be here and there. Jira can remain at
  high level... We will rely more upon code base and how we are moving forward
  with the PR and doing some automation such a way that when the code is
  getting updated, PR is getting moved, the Jira should move its status from in
  progress to done." And the scope valve, 00:34:30: "if we fail any of the
  epic, we should not be part of the MVP... we can park it outside, that will
  remain in the backlog."
- **The standup immediately after runs off the Jira board.** Rob asked at
  00:54:10; Rajeev agreed at 00:54:17.

## Board state at the start

Rajeev shared his screen and read the numbers off the summary page (00:02:05):
6 stories in progress, 2 done, 144 in the backlog, "and there can be more
additions in the due course". On the sprint board itself (00:02:58): 3 done, 3
in progress, 1 to do.

The three done are SCRIBL-4 (lay down the Claude Code harness in the new repo),
SCRIBL-75 (get the POC in line) and SCRIBL-78 (GitHub access). Rob's "it just
merged that this morning" (00:03:36) lands on the harness item, SCRIBL-4, which
Rajeev had just read out.

Rob's view, and it belongs in the Shape Review: the board undercounts the work.
00:25:32: "we did way more than the six tickets that are showing up in there.
We just weren't using the board. So let's get that updated because I'm going to
be giving that to the client and being like, hey, we did all this awesome
work."

## Device and OS support proposal (Shubhankar)

Still a proposal in the team channel, not yet a comment on the ticket.
Shubhankar, 00:10:03: "once we all are aligned to that, I'll just put the
comment in the ticket for review", and 00:10:19: "it's just a proposal state
right now."

- iOS 16 as the minimum supported version. 00:09:05: "we can go ahead with iOS
  16 as the base version because it covers 88% of the market as of now."
- iOS 26 as the primary target. 00:11:10: "more than 60% of the devices are
  already upgraded to 26. So that is like our go-to platform once we have
  backward testing with 16."
- Test across form factors, including a small one. iPhone SE 2nd gen, quoted as
  "4.5, 4.7 inch" (00:09:26). The reason is specific to this app, 00:11:30: "why
  I'm considering device form factor, because of our nature of application, like
  we have to draw something. So the visible space for end user, that should be
  properly usable."
- Device allocation, 00:12:09: developers on a regular device ("14, 15, or 13
  maybe"), QA on a lower-end device "to check all the bottlenecks or performance
  issues", and one high-end device for the team. He listed 14, 15, 16, 17 as the
  regular band earlier (00:09:26), so the dev-device numbers are not stated
  consistently.

Karuna asked whether the MVP should target a single version (00:10:38).
Shubhankar's answer is a minimum-to-latest range, not one version (00:10:50).

Pramod turned it into an action, 00:13:12: "we can make that recommendation of
like base version, latest version, and basically setting the expectations that
these will be the ones that we'll be focusing our testing on, maybe 3, 4
versions across this base to latest. And then we share it with Erik and group."
Rob, 00:13:36: "Let's get that in the meta repo as well. We'll have that
documented, create a page for it in the wiki. And then we can get that in front
of the client and then make sure they're approved."

## The moderation decision is reopened

Flagging this on its own because it reverses a prior team decision. Nitish,
00:26:28 to 00:27:05: "we actually decided not to have the moderation policy.
But when today I was working on something, moderation is something required by
the Apple itself for application to go live on the Apple, as discussed with
Pankaj. So I just need to discuss this ticket again with Pankaj once before
closing it."

If Apple requires moderation for App Store approval, "no moderation policy" is
not a decision the team gets to keep. Rajeev asked whether Nitish had time for
it today (00:27:06); the transcript records no answer.

Karuna, 00:49:38: "I was going through some of the user stories and epics as
